LESSON: KENYAN INDIGENOUS GAMES (OPTIONAL) BOARD GAMES

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS
Strand: Strand 11
Topic 11.2: Kenyan Indigenous Games (Optional) Board games
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Kenyan Indigenous Games (Optional) Board games, part of Strand 11 in Grade 9 CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS.

Key inquiry question: How do indigenous board games enhance mental relaxation? 2. Why are board games considered an indigenous game?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. watch a virtual or live demonstration of indigenous board games and identify the skills observed in the games,

2. demonstrate indigenous board game skills while observing safety,

3. practice skills in different indigenous board games while observing safety

4. play games using different indigenous board games with background musical rhythm. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. watch a virtual or live demonstration of indigenous board games and identify the skills observed in the games,
2. demonstrate indigenous board game skills while observing safety,
3. practice skills in different indigenous board games while observing safety
4. play games using different indigenous board games with background musical rhythm. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Kenyan Indigenous Games (Optional) Board games together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
• Responsibility: the learner takes on different roles during indigenous board games.

• Unity: the learner works with others in indigenous board games.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Safety: the learner observes safety rules when playing indigenous board games.

• Health and Fitness: the learner improves fitness through indigenous board games for a healthy lifestyle.

Link to other learning areas:

Mathematics: the learner keeps counting during indigenous board games.
